mix_frequency_estimate: CALL ~60-75%, RAISE (3-bet to ~38-44bb) ~20-35%, FOLD ~0-5%. Architect's CALL ~70% / RAISE ~30% framing sits inside the plausible-solver band; my central estimate is CALL ~65% / RAISE ~30% / FOLD <5%. The mix is genuine, not a label error.
reasoning:
BOARD VERIFICATION: Ts9d8s. Suits = T-spade, 9-diamond, 8-spade. Two-tone spades. Hero holds 8h 8c — neither hole card is a spade, so HERO HAS NO FLUSH DRAW. This is load-bearing: a common labelling trap on a two-tone board is to credit the set-holder with a redraw it does not have. The two spades live in villains' ranges, not ours.

MADE-HAND CLASS: Middle set of 8s (8h8c on T98 = three eights, with T and 9 as the over-cards on board). NOT bottom set in the absolute sense (bottom card of board is the 8, so set-of-8s is technically 'bottom set' by board-bottom-card convention — design memo §510 calls it bottom set; this is consistent terminology). Straights already complete: 67 = made straight (one combo per suit-pair, 16 combos pre-blockers). JQ and QJ make nut straight only on a J or Q turn; on the FLOP, the only made-straight class is 67 (T9876 with hero blocking the 8 — hero removes 2 of the 4 eights, leaving 67 combos drawn from 6 sevens × 4 sixes minus pair-blocking = ~24 combos but mostly suited/connector hands that fit preflop ranges: 76s, 67s, A6s-type rare). At 100bb 5-way limped-style pot with UTG opener + 3 flatters, 76s/67s ARE in CO's and BTN's flat ranges and in BB's defend range; UTG's open range carries 76s and possibly 67s thin.

DRAW CLASS for villains: any-two-spades = NFD if Ax-spade; OESD = QJ/J7/76 (J7 unlikely preflop, QJ in all flat ranges, 76 already made); gutters = J-anything-with-7-or-Q. The board hits the preflop-flat ranges hard: T9s, T8s, 98s are all two-pair combos; TT/99 are sets (88 in hero); JTs/QJs/KQs are overpair+OESD/gutter+overcard combos.

ACTION CHAIN READ: BB donk-leads 4bb (~32% pot) into 5-way. BB's donk range on T98ss after calling a 2.5bb UTG open in BB is heavily protection/equity-driven: 76s (made straight), T9s/98s (two pair), TT/99 (sets — though TT is sometimes 3-bet pre), J-something-spade-with-gutter, raw flush draws (Axs-spade, KQss, QJss-suited spade equity). BB donks because in 5-way with 4 villains seeing the flop, checking risks the pot being checked through with villains' draws and overcards. UTG (the preflop opener) RAISES to 14bb (3.5x donk, ~46% pot raise sizing). UTG's range face-up raises on this board: overpairs JJ-AA (some 3-bet pre, but JJ/QQ/KK definitely raise this donk for value+protection), TT/99 (sets — 88 in hero), AT/KT-suited (top-pair good kicker), and the rare made-straight 67s. UTG's raise range is NOT bluff-heavy in 5-way over a donk; UTG is announcing strong made hand or 2-pair+.

CO AND BTN STILL BEHIND: This is the load-bearing 5-way structural fact. If hero 3-bets to ~38-44bb, hero commits ~30bb on the flop and faces potential cold-calls or cold-4-bets from CO/BTN with sets-over (99/TT, since 88 is hero's), made straights (67s if in flat range), and combo-draws (NFD+OESD = J-spade-with-7 or Q-spade-with-J-spade). The squeeze-the-raise line builds a 100+bb pot OOP-to-position-behind with bottom-of-set range vs a raise-range tilted to higher sets and straights. Hero's set-of-8s has at minimum ~10 outs vs straights (one-out boats: turn 8 = quads; pair-the-board = T/9 = boat = 6 outs to T/9 minus dead; runner-runner blanks for showdown), so vs 67-made-straight equity is ~33% on flop, ~22% if turn bricks. Vs higher sets, hero is drawing to ~2 outs (the case 8 + runner-runner board-pair-pair). Vs overpairs/top-pair, hero is crushing.

EV DECOMPOSITION:
- CALL line: pot becomes ~44.5bb going to turn with 4 villains still possible (CO, BTN, BB) — though BB and CO/BTN must continue facing the raise + hero's flat. Realistic continuance: BB folds the raise often (~60%), UTG is committed, CO/BTN face 14bb cold-call which is 31% pot odds in a multiway with a raise-action-chain — CO/BTN continuance ~25% each with sets/straights/NFD+OESD. Expected pot at turn: ~50-65bb, hero closes flop action OOP-vs-UTG-in-position (UTG raised but acts before CO/BTN turn order — actually on turn, action order is BB→UTG→hero(MP)→CO→BTN, so hero acts THIRD on turn, with UTG facing turn lead and hero deciding to call/raise/lead-into-raiser). Set-of-8s equity vs UTG's raise-range that continues to turn ~40-50% (crushing overpairs, even-money vs 67, behind sets).
- RAISE line: pot becomes ~108bb with ~62bb behind if hero raises to ~44bb. Realistic continuance: UTG re-raises with sets/straight, calls with overpairs/2-pair; CO/BTN cold-call with sets/straights/NFD+OESD (rare cold-4-bet). Hero equity vs continuance range: behind sets-over and straights, ahead of overpairs and 2-pair. Net equity ~38-45%. Stack-off risk substantial; protection value real (denies turn equity to flush draws and overcards).
- FOLD: not a serious option. Set-of-8s vs donk-raise on T98ss has too much equity vs even the value-tightest continuance ranges. Fold-EV is strictly worse than call-EV.

GTO LENS ON THE CALL-vs-RAISE MIX: In solver outputs on similar 5-way coordinated-board set-on-bottom spots facing donk-raise chains, the modal play is CALL with a meaningful RAISE-for-protection minor mix. The CALL frequency is driven by (a) range-protection — hero needs a flatting range on this node that contains some sets to prevent UTG from polarizing the raise, and set-of-8s is the natural flat candidate since middle sets prefer CALL on draw-heavy boards where higher sets are the dominant raise-class; (b) position-behind capture — CO/BTN's draws + Tx/9x give dead money to hero's set when they overcall; (c) stack-preservation for turn play — hero realizes equity via implied-odds-on-boat-turns + fold-equity-on-spade-bricks. The RAISE frequency is driven by (a) protection vs the spade-flush-draw density (any two spades makes NFD vs hero); (b) charging dominated draws; (c) pot-building when hero's equity is realistically ~45% vs continuance.

KEY GTO CONSIDERATION (load-bearing for owner arbitration): The decision-relevant question is NOT whether CALL is +EV (it clearly is) — it is whether RAISE > CALL in EV. The answer depends almost entirely on the spade-draw density in BB/CO/BTN flat ranges. If solver assigns higher spade-draw weight to those ranges, RAISE frequency climbs toward ~40%. If solver assigns lower spade-draw weight (because preflop ranges are tight 5-way), RAISE frequency stays at ~25-30%. Architect's CALL ~70% / RAISE ~30% is right in the center of this band.

VERDICT: CALL. Confidence MEDIUM_HIGH on the modal action label (CALL is highest-frequency). Confidence MEDIUM on the precise mix. AGREE with architect. The CALL label survives owner-arbitration because RAISE is the genuine secondary action — never FOLD, never bet/lead-style action available since hero is facing a raise. If solver returns RAISE > 50%, the label should flip to RAISE with the spade-protection rationale; if solver returns CALL > 70%, architect's lean is confirmed cleanly.
